summary.text: Kweisi Mfume is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 7th Congressional District. A Baltimore native, he served on the Baltimore City Council and in the U.S. House from 1987 to 1996, led the NAACP for nine years, and returned to Congress by winning a 2020 special election. He advanced from the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 70.1% of the vote.

background.text: According to his congressional biography, he was born, raised and educated in Baltimore.

Graduated magna cum laude from Morgan State University, where he later taught as an adjunct professor, and earned a master's degree in liberal arts with a concentration in international studies from Johns Hopkins University.

Worked as an activist, radio commentator, administrator and television personality before winning his first election, to the Baltimore City Council, at age 31. He served on the council from 1978 to 1986 and chaired its Committee on Health Policy.

Represented Maryland's 7th District in the U.S. House from 1987 to 1996. His official biography lists service on the Banking and Financial Services, Education, Small Business and Ethics committees, chairmanship of the Joint Economic Committee, and chairmanship of the Congressional Black Caucus.
Left Congress in February 1996 to become president and chief executive officer of the NAACP, serving nine years.

After the NAACP, was executive director of the National Medical Association (from 2010) and led a National Institutes of Health-funded health policy research consortium in Maryland (2013 to 2018), according to his official biography.
Sworn in on May 5, 2020, after winning a special election to fill the term vacated by the death of Rep. Elijah Cummings, and was subsequently elected to full terms.

Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (ranking member of the Government Operations Subcommittee) and the Committee on Foreign Affairs. He is chairman of the Morgan State University Board of Regents.

priorities.text: Community involvement and public policy shaped by his decades in Baltimore civic life.
Protect Temporary Protected Status holders from deportation and pass the American Dream and Promise Act to provide TPS recipients and Dreamers an earned path to citizenship.
Sustain and expand Baltimore's Group Violence Reduction Strategy, which pairs law enforcement, social services and community partners to reduce shootings and homicides.

positions.summary: Said Republicans' $70 billion in additional ICE and CBP funding came with no reforms or oversight, that the agency needs reform and oversight rather than more money, and that he voted no.
positions.quote: what this agency needs is serious reform and meaningful oversight, not more money and a blank check from a Republican-controlled Congress that refuses to do its job

positions.summary: Joined the Maryland delegation in a letter urging House Republican leaders to extend the ACA enhanced premium tax credits and warning of Medicaid losses under H.R. 1.
positions.quote: we urge leadership to act swiftly to extend the ePTCs

record.text: As a Baltimore City Council member, chaired the Committee on Health Policy and led efforts to divest city funds from the apartheid government of South Africa.
Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and House Committee on Foreign Affairs for the 2025-2026 term.

candidates.name: Scott Collier

summary.text: Scott Collier is the Republican nominee for Maryland's 7th Congressional District. According to Ballotpedia, he is a Dundalk High School graduate who has worked as a structural steel painter, home improvement specialist and media entrepreneur. He has run for office several times since 2018 and was unopposed in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Graduated from Dundalk High School in 1981.
Professional experience includes work as a structural steel painter and home improvement specialist, and as a media entrepreneur with DundalkTV.
Ran for Maryland State Senate District 6 in 2018 as an unaffiliated candidate, receiving 4.6% of the vote.
Lost the 2020 Republican primary for Maryland's 2nd Congressional District.
Won the 2022 Republican primary for this seat and lost the general election to Rep. Kweisi Mfume, 82.1% to 17.7%; ran again in 2024 and lost, receiving 17.2% to Mfume's 80.3%.

priorities.text: In a 2018 Ballotpedia biographical submission: giving political power back to the people and working together on solutions.
In a 2024 questionnaire answer: addressing crime, gangs, education and drug problems in District 7.
priorities.quote: I want to work with the citizens of District 7 to turn the tide on crime, gangs, educational issues & the out of control drug problems

priorities.text: In a 2024 questionnaire answer: ending food deserts and working with law enforcement.
priorities.quote: Another priority is putting an end to food deserts in our communities.

positions.summary: Said in a 2024 questionnaire that Congress should not act to protect abortion rights after Dobbs, calling it a state's rights issue.
positions.quote: No. I believe that the Supreme Court made the correct decision, because this is a state's rights issue. I believe that life starts at conception.

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign website posts his answers to the Oct. 2024 Baltimore Sun questionnaire and says his priorities (economy, crime, education) are unchanged for 2026. Only the abortion answer squarely matches a guide topic; his Ukraine and Gaza answers are not guide issues. Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 survey.

researchNotes: Scott Collier has not reported federal campaign contributions in any of his prior runs and has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey for this or any recent race; his only stated priority comes from a 2018 candidate survey for a different office (Maryland State Senate). His research depth is marked minimal. Mfume's official site (mfume.house.gov) has no dedicated issues page; his positions here come from press releases on votes-and-legislation and media/press-releases. His press releases did not contain statements squarely matching the other 14 issue-key statements (e.g., his West Bank letter addresses settler violence and rule of law, not continued military aid to Israel, so it is not cited as an israel_aid position).
